name: Soren Cervantes-Delgado
role: Bootleg media seller and small-time data broker
location: The Alban Souk, Hamtramck Enclave, near Halsted and Chicago Ave
description:
Soren Cervantes-Delgado is a tall man gone slightly stooped with age, with a long, deeply lined face the color of dark walnut and close-cropped silver hair. He wears reading glasses with one cracked lens that he has refused to replace for reasons he won't fully explain, and his fingers are permanently ink-stained from a printer he still operates by hand. His stall in the Alban Souk is an organized labyrinth — physical media stacked in towers that somehow have internal logic only he can navigate, data-chips in labeled trays, printed zines in weathered portfolios, bootleg entertainment feeds on a slow-scroll display board behind him. He smells of old plastics, hot electronics, and a tobacco substitute he has smoked for forty years.

Soren Cervantes-Delgado does not move quickly and he does not need to. He has been in this spot, or a spot within fifty meters of this spot, for twenty-six years. He speaks with the careful economy of someone who has decided that most conversations don't require more than a hundred words, but when he talks about something he loves — old cinema, pre-Corponation literature, the acoustic properties of physical music formats — he becomes a completely different person, voluble and precise and slightly alarming in his enthusiasm. He knows what data passes through the Souk before almost anyone else does. He sells most of it. He keeps some of it. Nobody is quite sure which is which.

core_fears: Becoming irrelevant — a curiosity rather than a resource
The total disappearance of physical media and the histories they carry
core_desires: To keep knowledge alive that corporations would prefer be forgotten
To find one person worth passing his archive to
coping_mechanisms: Retreats into cataloguing and organization when emotionally overwhelmed
Uses historical analogy to distance himself from present pain
blind_spots: Romanticizes the past in ways that occasionally distort his reading of the present
His caution about sharing certain data sometimes shades into hoarding — he tells himself it's protective
psychology.secret: He holds a partial archive of pre-corporate land records for Hamtramck and three adjacent zones — documentation that could legally complicate several Corponation territorial claims. He received it from a dying archivist twenty years ago. He has never shown it to anyone. He believes that information this significant is also a death warrant for whoever holds it, and he cannot decide if that means he should destroy it, share it, or keep it safe until the right moment arrives.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Formal and unhurried. Dense with historical reference and analogy. Does not use current slang unless he's quoting someone. Occasionally drops into Guinean French cadences when thinking hard.
speech_patterns.cadence: Slow and considered. Long pauses between thoughts that do not feel like hesitation — more like he's selecting carefully. Will not be rushed.
verbal_tics: 'There was a film once—' as a way of introducing almost any observation
Adjusts his cracked glasses when he's deciding whether to trust someone
Uses 'naturally' to acknowledge things other people think are surprising
example_lines: 'There was a film once — 2041, I think, pre-Axiom — about exactly this kind of arrangement. It ended badly for the man who knew too much and well for the man who knew how to forget. I've always found that instructive.'
'Naturally, I have what you're looking for. Whether I should sell it to you is a different question, and it will take a moment.'

story_hooks: He has identified a data-chip in a recent shipment that was clearly not intended for open sale — it came with a specific zine order from a supply contact who has since stopped responding to communications.
Someone has visited the stall twice asking, very casually, whether he carries historical land records. They didn't buy anything. He needs to know who sent them.

A young community organizer in Hamtramck has been researching corporate land claims and has gotten close enough to the truth that Faustin thinks she'll either find the archive independently or get hurt looking. He is considering whether to make contact.
narrative_function: Information broker, cultural repository, and reflective background presence. Characters who need data, obscure pre-Corponation records, or someone who remembers what the city looked like before come to Faustin. He's also the most reliable source for understanding context — what an event means, what it echoes from the past.
augmentations: Retinal display overlay — old model, first generation, occasionally glitches. Memory-index augmentation — helps him catalogue and retrieve his inventory; he also uses it for everything else. Nothing cosmetic.
daily_life: Opens his stall at 0900 after a slow morning reading. Stays until 2000. Rarely leaves the Souk for anything beyond supply runs to his two physical media sources. Eats at the same noodle stand every day.
affiliation: Independent; nominal membership in The Oxidian Market Vendors Guild (honorary, pays no dues); long-standing informal arrangement with a Hamtramck Enclave community council

decision_rules: Never sell data he hasn't personally verified
Don't discuss the archive under any circumstances — including when not discussing it becomes conspicuous
Give younger vendors in the Souk fair prices on their goods; the market is better when everyone can survive in it
escalation_ladder: Quiet and complete unresponsiveness — effective stonewalling
Refers the problem to Souk community council without explaining why
Closes the stall and is simply not there

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Measured and formal — assesses by what they ask for and how they ask it. Generous with casual customers, thoughtful about anyone who wants data.
interpersonal_modes.friends: Warm in a reserved way. Remembers everything about them. Asks questions rather than volunteering feelings.

stress_responses.low: Reorganizes a section of his catalogue
stress_responses.medium: Becomes extremely precise and formal in speech
stress_responses.high: Goes physically still and entirely silent — processes internally, responds much later

contradictions: Believes information should be free, but controls his own archive with extreme care
Presents as detached from politics but has been quietly enabling opposition to Corponation encroachment for decades
habits: Cleans and inspects every piece of physical media before shelving it
Mutters titles and catalog numbers while working — partially for the stall's ELF, which he treats as the true keeper of the inventory
Rereads the same three novels on rotation
breaking_points: Witnessing the deliberate destruction of cultural or historical records
Someone threatening a Souk vendor who can't defend themselves

physical_description.heritage: Hispanic/Latin American (57.5%) with significant Sub-Saharan African (22.0%) and South Asian (20.5%) ancestry. This creates a richly complex phenotype combining warm golden and amber undertones from Latin American heritage with deeper melanin-rich undertones from Sub-Saharan ancestry and the luminous quality characteristic of South Asian skin. The blend produces a distinctive warm medium-to-dark brown complexion with subtle ochre and bronze notes.
physical_description.build: Tall and lean, slightly stooped through the shoulders from decades hunched over inventory and printing equipment. Still carries a wiry frame despite age; no excess weight but visible muscle atrophy in the upper back.
physical_description.hair_style: Close-cropped, neatly trimmed but not fussy
physical_description.eye_color: Dark brown, natural; right eye shows faint grid pattern overlay artifact from first-generation retinal display
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm medium-to-dark brown with golden amber undertones. Deeply weathered with age, the complexion carries the richness of blended heritage — Latin American warmth, Sub-Saharan depth, and South Asian luminosity converging into a distinctive ochre-bronze patina. Age spots visible on temples and cheekbones show characteristic melanin patterning of darker skin aging.
physical_description.complexion: Deeply lined face with prominent creases around the eyes and mouth; weathered but clean-shaven. Facial structure reflects the blend of Latin American and Sub-Saharan heritage with warm, rounded features and strong bone structure characteristic of the genetic mix. Small age spots on the temples and cheekbones. One cracked lens of reading glasses worn habitually — the left lens has a vertical hairline fracture he refuses to repair. Permanent ink stains on the tips of all fingers, darkest on thumb and forefinger. Minor tobacco staining at the corners of his mouth.
distinguishing_marks: A thin, pale scar runs along the left jawline from ear toward chin, approximately 8 centimeters, consistent with old blunt-force trauma; rarely mentioned when asked.
Ink-black burn scar on the inside of his left wrist, roughly 3 centimeters across, shaped like a printer's heat plate — deliberate, self-inflicted, from an accident he reframed as a lesson.
Deep creases and calluses across both palms from manual printing work, left hand showing heavier wear.
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Retinal display overlay visible as faint iridescent grid in the right eye when light catches it at certain angles; occasional micro-stuttering of the eyelid when the system glitches. No other visible chrome or cosmetic mods. The memory-index augmentation is purely internal, invisible.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves with deliberate slowness, never rushed. Economy of gesture — when he reaches for something, the movement is precise and minimal. Tends to lean slightly forward when listening, hands often resting flat on his counter or folded in his lap. His gaze is sharp despite the age; he observes more than he moves.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3-4 working class, carefully maintained but intentionally plain. Favors loose linen shirts in neutral tones (cream, gray, pale brown), often with the sleeves rolled to the elbow. Wears a long canvas apron over his clothes, multiple pockets reinforced and stained with use. Dark cotton trousers, well-fitted but worn. Leather slip-on shoes, repaired multiple times, comfortable and broken-in. A faded jacket — possibly from the 2190s — hangs near his stall for cooler days. No jewelry except a plain metal band on his right ring finger. Habitually carries a cloth handkerchief for wiping dust off inventory.
